analysis.title: markets / macro (Tony Pasquariello, 31 Oct 2026)
key_insights: S&P fell 57 bps on the week (SPW, the equal-weight index, rose 80 bps). The desk says this hides heavy churn under the surface in the market's most important theme, and that October combined a modest index move with difficult risk management along the way.

Index returns versus the GS flagship momentum basket (GSPRHIMO) in the second half of 2026: S&P -0.13% (July), +2.62% (August), -0.45% (September), -0.93% (October). GSPRHIMO -30.19% (July), -13.67% (August), +26.96% (September), -18.60% (October). The S&P is going nowhere while single-stock, sector and thematic moves are large.

Desk view: the primary bull trend remains intact, but the market will deliver less upside power and sub-surface volatility is here to stay. On risk/reward the author quotes 'the big bets always appear, but I'm not making them right now.'

Q3 tech earnings are expected to be remembered as a disappointment despite a handful of cloud businesses compounding huge growth rates on huge denominators. Hyperscaler capex intentions are clearly not slowing, while a few of the big names missed somewhere in the core of their business.

The desk expects the bull market to continue in 2027 with less punch, with more confidence after this week. S&P earnings have been superb, but earnings growth appears to have peaked and the rate of upgrades to forward estimates has slowed versus recent reporting cycles.

For the next two months the technicals favor bulls for three reasons: sentiment is unequivocally downbeat (off-the-shelf measures and client conversations), the seasonal swing from the worst stretch of the year (mid-August to mid-October) to the best (mid-October to year-end) is underway, and the market spent the past month clearing a significant amount of length. The bear counter is that the same was said into late 2018.
This week's Fed meeting was uneventful and was barely a topic of conversation among stock operators.

Oil has built significant risk premium into the midterms (COZ6 is at its dead highs), while European equities rose again and the Swiss SMI hit record highs. The author declines to force an explanation for the divergence.
The desk agrees with increasing commodities allocation. With BCOM up 28% YTD, GS recently made both a tactical and a structural bull case for commodities.

US mega cap tech has had three very tough weeks. The 4th largest company in the S&P just had its single worst day ever as a public company, while the broader trend in S&P ex-AI is the contrast the author charts.
